citation.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Model-based Optimization Method for Graphic Design
citation.venue: Informatica (Slovenia) 48(5), 2024, pp. 121-134 (pages from the PDF header; volume and issue from Crossref; online 2024-04-08). Diamond open access, CC BY per OpenAlex
citation.version_coded: Version of record: publisher PDF (14 pages) from informatica.si, the open copy that OpenAlex lists, read in full as text; pp. 126 and 130 also checked on the rendered pages

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded as FT-NOBASELINE). The article describes neural-network density fields for compliance and stress-constrained TO but reports no TO result; its only comparisons are computation-time percentages, accuracy, precision and recall against three interior-layout methods (MDP, VR, AI).
claim.location: Abstract; Sec. 4.2-4.5 (method); Sec. 5, Tables 3-6 and Figs. 5-8 (results); Sec. 7 (conclusion)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded). Table 3 lists 'computation time (%)' of 61 for the proposed method vs 91, 73 and 81 for MDP, VR and AI, with no definition, unit base or problem; the abstract restates it as 61 s.

notes: Excluded under PROTOCOL §4 and the FT-NOBASELINE clarification of 2026-09-24. Codes checked in order. FT-DUPLICATE: no other version in the pool (title searched). FT-SCOPE: not applied, because the proposed method (Sec. 4.2-4.5) is density-based TO with a feed-forward network density field, a compliance objective and a p-norm stress constraint, although the results concern graphic and interior layout; a verifier may prefer FT-SCOPE on that basis. FT-TYPE, FT-DOMAIN, FT-NOML and FT-FORWARD: do not apply. FT-MLONLY: does not apply, because the article calls two of its three comparators 'conventional' or 'standard' methods (Sec. 5.1-5.2). FT-NOBASELINE applies: no classical TO or homogenization-based method is run, timed or cited with a cost or result. The comparators are MDP = Ran & Dong 2022 (multiobjective building-interior design), VR = Wu 2022 (interior layout with VR and 5G) and AI = Di & Yu 2021 (multi-agent RL furniture layout) [from the reference list]. They address interior layout, not TO, and are scored on accuracy, precision and recall defined from true and false positives (Eqs. 18-20), which have no TO meaning. The 2D and 3D compliance and stress-constrained results that the abstract announces appear nowhere in the text: no design, compliance value, volume or iteration count is reported, and Figs. 3-4 show network diagrams and building images. SIMP appears only as qualitative motivation (Sec. 4.2), and conclusion (a) says the network needs far fewer design variables than voxel-based optimization, without numbers. The abstract gives the computation time as 61 s, while Table 3 gives 61 (%). Hardware: 64-bit Intel Xeon Gold 2.10 GHz server, Python 3.7, TensorFlow 2.0.0 (Sec. 5). Screening code was I-UNCLEAR. Authors checked: no author named Jun Wang. Adjudicator check (2026-09-24): the version-of-record PDF (14 pages) was re-read in full from the publisher's own file host (informatica.si article/download/5295/2669, the citation_pdf_url of the article page). The text confirms the first coder's reading: Sec. 5 (p. 129) names MDP (Ran & Dong 2022), VR (Wu 2022) and AI (Di & Yu 2021) as comparators, and Sec. 5.1-5.2 (p. 130) call VR and MDP 'standard' and 'conventional' methods, so the comparison is not ML-only; none of the three is a TO or homogenization-based optimizer (reference list [8], [14], [21], pp. 132-133).

ft_code.reason: FT-MLONLY needs a comparison with ML methods only, but the article itself calls two of its three comparators, VR and MDP, 'standard' and 'conventional' methods (Sec. 5.1-5.2, p. 130); only AI (Di & Yu 2021) is an RL method. None of the three is a TO or homogenization-based optimizer (interior-layout papers, references [8], [14], [21]), and SIMP appears only as motivation (Sec. 4.2, p. 126), so no classical method's cost or result is cited: FT-NOBASELINE, the next code in table order.
